subject.title: Bound HTTP error body snippets to readable streams

question: Should OpenClaw formally treat an empty snippet as the contract for responses that cannot expose a cancellable readable stream, even when a foreign adapter offers diagnostic text through an unbounded `text()` method?
rationale: The code cannot safely bound a whole-body-only API, but choosing memory safety over shipped diagnostic text is a compatibility and failure-boundary decision that requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept fail-closed snippets
options.body: Adopt the PR's empty-snippet contract for non-readable adapters and rely on HTTP status, headers, and bounded readable streams for diagnostics.

options.title: Require a bounded adapter contract
options.body: Hold the PR until foreign adapters can provide an explicitly bounded prefix API without using whole-body `text()` or `arrayBuffer()` methods.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed snippets
recommendation.body: Adopt the PR's empty-snippet contract for non-readable adapters and rely on HTTP status, headers, and bounded readable streams for diagnostics.
